name: Mikey Ku Collection
note: demo is the index tile. variants, sizes, uses and motion fill the element's own page. sizes:true wraps sizeDemo in .mk-sm/.mk-md/.mk-lg — the size classes cascade, so nothing per-element is needed.

items.name: Buttons
items.note: Four weights of one shape. Everything that gives a button its character here is motion, not decoration: it lifts 2px on hover and a trailing arrow walks 3px with it. No glow, no fill flash, no shadow at rest.

variants.label: With arrow
variants.demo: <button class='mk-btn mk-btn--primary'>View projects <svg width='16' height='16' viewBox='0 0 24 24' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round'><path d='M5 12h14M12 5l7 7-7 7'/></svg></button>

motion.label: Hover lift
motion.note: The whole reason it reads as pressable. Nothing else changes.

motion.label: Arrow walk
motion.note: Only the trailing glyph moves. A leading icon stays put.

motion.label: Press
motion.note: Returns to the resting plane rather than pushing below it.

uses.label: Form footer
uses.note: Ghost for the way out, primary for the way forward.

uses.label: Page call to action
uses.note: The arrow earns its place when the button leads somewhere.

uses.label: Toolbar
uses.note: One .mk-sm on the row sizes every control inside it.

uses.label: Destructive row
uses.note: Danger stays quiet until you are actually over it.
uses.demo: Delete this project

items.name: Inputs
items.note: Field padding is 60% of the button's, because a field needs less inset than a label does. All three heights come from the same size vocabulary, so an input beside a button always lines up.

variants.label: Textarea
variants.demo: <textarea class='mk-textarea' placeholder='What should the reader know?'></textarea>

variants.label: With label
variants.demo: Shown on the card and the detail page.

motion.label: Border on hover
motion.note: Line to line-strong. The field acknowledges the cursor without moving.

motion.label: Focus ring
motion.note: Same treatment as every other focusable thing in the system.

uses.label: Labelled field
uses.note: Label, control and hint wired with aria-describedby.
uses.demo: Found on the top right of the estimate.

uses.label: Inline search
uses.note: Small size, so the pair sits inside a toolbar without crowding it.

uses.label: Filter row
uses.note: Select and button share a height because they share a size token.

items.name: Selection
items.note: Switch for things that apply the moment you touch them, checkbox for things you submit. Getting that distinction wrong is the most common reason a settings page feels untrustworthy.

variants.label: Checkbox

motion.label: Knob travel
motion.note: Track colour fills over the same duration, so the two read as one motion.

motion.label: Check draw
motion.note: The tick strokes itself in along its own path instead of popping into place.

uses.label: Settings list
uses.note: Switches, because each one takes effect immediately.

uses.label: Review list
uses.note: Checkboxes, because nothing happens until you submit.

items.name: Badges
items.note: Half a control's height and 85% of its text size, so a badge beside a small button and one beside a large button stay in proportion without anyone deciding a pixel value.
items.demo: In progressv0.6.0

uses.label: Beside a title
uses.note: Sized down so it never competes with the heading.
uses.demo:
Ground Truth

uses.label: Status column
uses.note: Dot plus word — status is never colour alone.
uses.demo: Shipped Draft

items.name: Loading
items.note: Dots when you have no idea what is coming, shimmer when you already know its shape. Reaching for a spinner where a skeleton would do is what makes an app feel slower than it is.

variants.label: Shimmer

motion.label: Dot bounce
motion.note: The stagger is what makes three dots read as one object rather than three.

motion.label: Shimmer sweep
motion.note: Built from the line tokens, so it stays visible on any surface.

motion.label: Reduced motion
motion.note: Not disabled — the dots hold at 0.7 opacity so the state is still legible.

uses.label: Busy button
uses.note: The spinner inherits the button's text colour, so no extra styling.

uses.label: Card placeholder
uses.note: Shimmer matched to the shape that will replace it.

items.name: Indicator slide
items.note: One element travels between options instead of a background jumping between them. Width animates too, so uneven labels still land clean — which is the part most implementations get wrong.

variants.label: Two options
Uneven labels

motion.label: Travel
motion.note: Position is written as a custom property from the active option's offsetLeft.

motion.label: Width
motion.note: Animated alongside, so uneven labels never cause a snap at the end.

motion.label: Re-measure
motion.note: Widths shift when fonts land or the container resizes; measuring once is not enough.

uses.label: View switch
uses.note: Sits above a list and changes how it renders.

items.name: Label swap
items.note: Both labels sit in one grid cell and crossfade past each other, so the button never changes width mid-swap. That width twitch is the tell that separates a considered copy button from a thrown-together one.

motion.label: Out
motion.note: The old label leaves upward.

motion.label: In
motion.note: The new one arrives from below, in the accent.

motion.label: Reset
motion.note: Long enough to register, short enough that you can copy twice.

uses.label: Beside a token
uses.note: Small size so it sits inside a code row without dominating it.
uses.demo: --accent

items.name: Toast in / out
items.note: Rises and scales in, holds, then falls away. The exit is deliberately shorter than the entrance — arriving should announce itself, leaving should not.

motion.label: Enter
motion.note: Rises and settles rather than sliding flat.

motion.label: Hold
motion.note: Long enough to read a short sentence without rushing.

motion.label: Exit
motion.note: Shorter than the entrance, and removed on animationend rather than a second timer.

uses.label: After an action
uses.note: Confirms something that already happened; never asks for a response.

items.name: Meter fill
items.note: Grows to its value rather than appearing at it. Costs one frame and makes the number feel measured instead of asserted — which matters a lot when the number is a model's confidence.

motion.label: Fill
motion.note: Two nested requestAnimationFrame calls before setting the width, or the browser collapses both styles into one paint and nothing animates.

uses.label: Confidence readout
uses.note: Label, value and bar — the bar is the fastest read, the number is the precise one.
